## Definition

An **effect size** quantifies the magnitude of an effect, independent of sample size. While p-values tell us if an effect exists, effect sizes tell us how large the effect is.

## Why Effect Sizes Matter

| p-value | Effect size |
|---------|-------------|
| Tells if effect is statistically significant | Tells if effect is practically meaningful |
| Depends heavily on sample size | Independent of sample size |
| Binary decision (significant/not) | Continuous measure |
| Can be "significant" but tiny | Reveals real-world importance |

## Common Effect Size Measures

| Statistic | Type | Formula |
|-----------|------|---------|
| Cohen's d | Standardised mean difference | $d = \frac{\bar{X}_1 - \bar{X}_2}{s_{pooled}}$ |
| Pearson's r | Correlation | Ranges -1 to +1 |
| Eta-squared ($\eta^2$) | Variance explained | $\frac{SS_{effect}}{SS_{total}}$ |
| Odds ratio | Categorical | Ratio of odds |

## Cohen's d Guidelines

| d value | Interpretation |
|---------|----------------|
| 0.2 | Small effect |
| 0.5 | Medium effect |
| 0.8 | Large effect |

Note: These are rough guidelines, not rigid cutoffs. Context matters.

## Correlation Guidelines

| r value | Interpretation |
|---------|----------------|
| .10 | Small |
| .30 | Medium |
| .50 | Large |

## R Code Example

```r
library(effectsize)

# Cohen's d for independent groups
cohens_d(score ~ group, data = mydata)

# Cohen's d for paired samples
cohens_d(condition_a, condition_b, paired = TRUE)

# Convert t-value to d
t_to_d(t = 2.45, df_error = 28)

# Interpret effect size
interpret_d(0.65)
```

## Reporting Effect Sizes

Always report effect sizes alongside significance tests:

> The treatment group scored significantly higher than the control group, *t*(58) = 3.21, *p* = .002, **d = 0.82** [0.28, 1.35].

Include 95% confidence intervals when possible.

## Effect Size vs. Statistical Significance

```
                    Effect Size
                 Small       Large
              ┌─────────┬─────────┐
Significant   │ Large n │ True    │
p < .05       │ needed  │ finding │
              ├─────────┼─────────┤
Non-signif.   │ True    │ Under-  │
p > .05       │ null    │ powered │
              └─────────┴─────────┘
```

## DataLab Connection

When reporting results from any DataLab station, calculate and interpret effect sizes. A "significant" difference in reaction times means little without knowing the magnitude.
